 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. New Zealand host India in the opening T20I of a five-match series at Hagley Oval on Thursday, October 22. It is the start of a 12-match tour that runs through to December 1.
 There is an obvious edge to the fixture. The last time these sides met, India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the T20 World Cup final in March, and Mitchell Santner's team will not have forgotten how comprehensively that night went against them.

 India are without Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya, while New Zealand have lost Rachin Ravindra to a dislocated shoulder along with Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes, which has thinned out both attacks before a ball has been bowled.
 Conditions could be the decisive factor at a ground India have never played a men's T20I on. The evening is forecast to stay dry but cold, with temperatures dropping towards 14°C by the closing overs.
 Live scorecard 
 New Zealand vs. India 1st T20I: Live updates and toss result
 India batting updates
 After 19.4 overs, India are 230/6 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A breathtaking finish spearheaded by Naman Dhir's blistering 42* off 15 balls and a calculated knock from Shreyas Iyer (42 off 28) saw India pull off their highest-ever successful run chase in T20I history, gunning down New Zealand's 225/4 with four wickets and two balls to spare at Hagley Oval, Christchurch.
 After 16 overs, India are 178/5 
 Sanju Samson's blistering knock ended after a dominant 67 off 33 balls, triggering a cluster of wickets as the Black Caps' spinners squeezed the scoring rate and stalled India's early momentum. Despite quick strikes removing the dangerous middle order, Shreyas Iyer anchored the innings with an unbeaten 33 off 22 balls, alongside newly arrived Naman Dhir (2*).
 After 10 overs, India are 119/3 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement New Zealand's spin duo of Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell pulled the Black Caps right back into the contest after India's electric Powerplay start. Samson was undone by a slow cutter off Santner that held in the pitch, ending a stellar knock of 67 that included eight boundaries and four sixes.
 Tilak Varma's painful stay at the crease ended shortly after, as he holed out to deep mid-wicket off Bracewell to leave India 119/3. With the required rate sitting at 10.70, newly arrived batters Shreyas Iyer and Ishan Kishan must rebuild quickly to keep India on track in this high-scoring chase.
 After 6 overs, New Zealand are 94/1 
 India's chase of 226 got off to a roaring start at Hagley Oval as Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma capitalised on a barrage of extras and loose line and length from New Zealand's seamers. The Powerplay produced an incredible 94 runs, keeping the required run rate well below the initial target of 11.30.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Despite losing Abhishek Sharma for a quickfire 29 in the final over of the Powerplay, India hold total control of the required rate. Sanju Samson remains unbeaten on 50 alongside Tilak Varma (1*), leaving India needing 132 runs from 84 balls with nine wickets in hand as the middle overs begin.
 New Zealand batting updates
 After 20 overs, New Zealand are 225/4 
 New Zealand mounted an absolute batting masterclass at Christchurch, recording their highest ever T20I team score on home soil by finishing at 225/4. Glenn Phillips proved to be the architect of the assault, blasting a magnificent 82* off 40 balls, ably supported by late blitzes from debutant Bevon Jacobs (31) and Finn Allen (45) at the top of the order.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement India's bowling attack found little joy in the death overs, with Mayank Yadav (1/40), Arshdeep Singh (1/45), and Axar Patel (1/51) all taking heavy punishment. A late run-out courtesy of Arshdeep Singh's footwork was one of the few bright spots in a tough fielding display. Set a mammoth target of 226, India's power-packed batting lineup will need an explosive start in the Powerplay to pull off a sensational chase.
 After 15 overs, New Zealand are 158/3 
 The Black Caps maintain a blistering scoring rate of 10.53, navigating through India's middle overs to reach 158/3 at the end of the 15th. Despite Arshdeep Singh making a breakthrough to send back Daryl Mitchell for 28, India's bowlers have struggled to contain the boundary flow.
 Glenn Phillips capitalised on sloppy fielding and full tosses, smashing Axar Patel for three boundaries in the 14th over to bring the spinner's spell to a painful close. Debutant Bevon Jacobs showed no big-stage nerves, dispatching Arshdeep for a towering six on debut to keep the hosts firmly on target for a daunting 200-plus total in Christchurch.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After 10 overs, New Zealand are 98/2 
 India's bowling unit effectively clawed their way back into the contest during the middle-over phase in Christchurch. With Finn Allen threatening to take total control of the innings after his 24-ball 45, Axar Patel struck the decisive blow, inducing a false shot that was safely taken at deep long-off.
 The tandem of Axar Patel and Nitish Kumar Reddy expertly checked the run rate, preventing further boundary damage and dropping the current run rate under 9.50. With Glenn Phillips (10*) joining Daryl Mitchell (15*) at the crease, the Black Caps hold crucial wickets in hand to construct a massive finish over the remaining ten overs.
 After 6 overs, New Zealand are 65/1 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement New Zealand made full use of the Powerplay, putting India's bowling attack under relentless pressure from the start. Tim Seifert and Finn Allen took on Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Arshdeep Singh, boundaries flowing freely despite some early lateral movement.
 Mayank Yadav provided India's sole breakthrough in the fifth over, using his express pace to get Seifert (24) caught behind by Sanju Samson. However, the momentum stayed with the hosts as Allen (33*) and Mitchell (7*) closed out the sixth over with a 16-run assault against Axar Patel.
 Toss result
 India won the toss and chose to field first.
